titulo: Safe batch operations: dry-run, marker, and dirty repository
lead: Adding a link back in forty repositories, swapping a footer on a hundred pages, fixing a canonical across the whole site: this is where the agent saves you hours, and this is where one mistake spreads. Three protections solve almost everything: show before you do, don't duplicate, and don't touch what someone else is working on.
objetivo: run an operation across several repositories with a dry-run, a marker against duplicating, and skipping dirty repos, checking by sample.

aprende.t: Dry-run by default: see what it would do before doing it
Skip the repository with unsaved work
Check it live by sample after the push

hero_alt: A woman sorts stacks of paper into wooden pigeonholes, with a separate box on its side on the table.

secoes.titulo: The path of a safe batch

nos.detalhe: A list of what will change and where: repository, link destination, label. The agent builds it; you read it. It's the scope of the batch in writing.
With no options at all, the script only tells you what it would do in each repository: DRY (would go in), PULA (skipped, with the reason), or OK (already there). Nothing is written.
Check the PULA entries and the destination files. A repository skipped because of a dirty working tree belongs to another session: don't force it.
--apply writes to the file; --commit also commits and pushes. A push is publishing: go through the gate before using --commit.
Open a few published pages and confirm the block in the HTML. At INEMA, the Oct 5 batch was checked on GitHub Pages by sample: 8 out of 8.

secoes.legenda: Three protections: dry-run, marker, and skipping a dirty repository.

texto: The script's default is not to write. Writing requires asking for it: --apply. That way a mistake in the map shows up in the list, not on the site.
Ask any agent for the same thing: first the list of what it would do, then the run.
The written block goes between two comments with the marker link-de-volta:v1. Before writing, the script looks for the marker: if it's already there, it answers "OK: já tinha".
This is what lets you run it again after a failure without creating two links on the same page.
If the repository has an uncommitted change, the script skips it. It's almost always another session (yours or another agent's) working on it.
It also skips a repository that's not on the expected branch and one that has no HTML. In INEMA, repositories skipped because of a dirty working tree were left for the next round.

If index.html is just a redirect (meta refresh), the link goes on the destination page. If the HTML is generated by a script, the link goes in the generator, otherwise it disappears on the next build.
In INEMA: 35 of 40 repositories on 09/24, another 25 on 10/02, and another 21 on 10/05.

secoes.sub: Swap the paths and destinations for your own.

blocos.rot: Dry-run, apply, and (after the gate) commit
blocos.conteudo:
python3 tools/link_de_volta.py mapa.json             # dry-run: só mostra
python3 tools/link_de_volta.py mapa.json --apply     # grava, sem commit
python3 tools/link_de_volta.py mapa.json --apply --commit   # grava, commita e faz push

Build the mapa.json with the repositories from the list and run link_de_volta.py with NO options (dry-run).
Show me the full output and stop.
Don't use --apply or --commit until I reply "aplica".
Repository with PULA: don't force it, don't stash, don't commit for it. Just tell me which one it is.

abas.html:
$ python3 tools/link_de_volta.py mapa.json
repos/curso-pao: DRY: entraria em index.html
repos/curso-cafe: PULA: alterações não commitadas
repos/curso-queijo: OK: já tinha
repos/curso-vinho: DRY: entraria em landing.html

$ python3 tools/link_de_volta.py mapa.json --apply
repos/curso-pao: APLICADO em index.html
repos/curso-cafe: PULA: alterações não commitadas
repos/curso-queijo: OK: já tinha
repos/curso-vinho: APLICADO em landing.html

Four test repositories set up for the lesson.

• curso-pao: clean, gets the block in index.html.
  • curso-cafe: has an unsaved change; skipped in both rounds.
  • curso-queijo: the marker was already there; nothing changes.
  • curso-vinho: index.html is just a redirect, so the block goes in landing.html.

After --apply without --commit, curso-pao and curso-vinho are left with an uncommitted change: running again without committing makes the script skip both. Commit or discard before the next round.

secoes.titulo: See the batch with interruption and resume
secoes.sub: Run it, interrupt halfway, and run it again. What's already done isn't redone.

msg.inicio: 5 repositories in the batch. Click "Run the batch".
msg.rodando: Applying one repository at a time. The block goes in with the marker link-de-volta:v1.
msg.parou: Interrupted. The middle repository was left in applying/. Run it again to see the resume.
msg.retoma: Resume: what was in applying/ went back to the queue. What already has the marker answers "OK: já tinha" and isn't redone.
msg.fim: Full batch: all with the marker.
msg.fimfalha: Full batch, with one repository skipped: uncommitted changes. It belongs to another session; you sort it out with whoever is working on it.

secoes.legenda: Illustrative simulation in the browser: nothing is actually written. The skip is on purpose, to show the dirty repository.

secoes.titulo: Practice: a real batch, over the network
secoes.sub: Use 3 or more of your own repositories (or create test repositories with a simple index.html).

exercicios.texto: Ask the agent for the mapa.json and the dry-run, using the request above. Leave one repository with an uncommitted change on purpose.
exercicios.pronto: the output shows at least one DRY and one PULA with the reason, and the git status of the repositories did not change.

exercicios.texto: Reply "aplica", run with --apply, check the diff of each repository, commit (or use --commit), and run the dry-run again.
exercicios.pronto: the second run answers "OK: já tinha" in the repositories you applied, and you opened at least 2 published pages and saw the link in the HTML.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: What does link_de_volta.py do when you run it with no options?
opcoes: It shows what it would do in each one, without writing anything.
perguntas.explica: Dry-run is the default. Writing requires --apply; publishing requires --commit. The common mistake is the reverse: a script that writes by default and needs an option to simulate.

perguntas.p: A repository shows up as "PULA: alterações não commitadas". What should you do?
opcoes: Leave it for later: it's probably another session working on it.
perguntas.explica: An unsaved change is someone's work. Forcing it mixes your commit with theirs. In INEMA, the skipped ones were left for the next round.

perguntas.p: What is the link-de-volta:v1 marker for?
opcoes: So you can run it again without duplicating the block.
So the script can find the footer.
perguntas.explica: Before writing, the script looks for the marker. If it already exists, it answers "OK: já tinha". That is what makes resuming safe.

perguntas.p: A course's index.html is just a redirect. Where should the link go?
perguntas.explica: The search engine follows the redirect and reads the destination. A link in the redirect file is not seen. If the HTML is generated, the link goes in the generator.

itens.texto: See the list first; write only with --apply.
Running twice does not duplicate; resuming is safe.
A repository with an unsaved change is skipped, not forced.
--commit does a push: go through the gate before it and check a sample after.
